title: Small models of quotient maps from a fixed module sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O_X$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and let module sheaves and their morphisms mean those of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. All sets of points and sections are taken in a fixed Grothendieck universe, and the index sets below are in that universe. Fix an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal M$. There are a set $T$, modules $Q_t$ and epimorphisms $q_t:\mathcal M\to Q_t$ for $t\in T$ such that for every module $\mathcal N$ and epimorphism $p:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ there are $t\in T$ and an isomorphism $\psi:Q_t\to\mathcal N$ with $\psi\circ q_t=p$. One may take $T$ to be the set of all literal subsheaves of modules $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal M$ (specified by submodules $\mathcal K(W)\subseteq\mathcal M(W)$ stable under restriction and satisfying the sheaf axiom), and $q_{\mathcal K}$ to be the cokernel of the inclusion $\mathcal K\to\mathcal M$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$.

source.place: Tag 01BC (lemma-set-isomorphism-classes-finite-type-modules), proof: parametrization by kernel subsheaves, generalized from the fixed finite-free source to a fixed module sheaf

proof.text: Let $\mathcal U$ be the fixed universe. Since $X\in\mathcal U$, its set $\operatorname{Op}(X)\subseteq\mathcal P(X)$ belongs to $\mathcal U$. The product $\prod_{W\in\operatorname{Op}(X)}\mathcal P(\mathcal M(W))$ is therefore a set in $\mathcal U$. Let $T$ be its subset consisting of families $K(W)$ that are submodules, are stable under restriction, and satisfy the sheaf axiom. These conditions select a subset of a set. The operations and restriction maps of a literal subsheaf are inherited from $\mathcal M$, so such a family determines exactly one literal module subsheaf $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal M$; no additional unbounded choices of structure are needed.

source.place: Tag 01BC, lemma-set-isomorphism-classes-finite-type-modules, proof: parametrization by kernel subsheaves; Tag 01AG, lemma-abelian, and preceding kernel/cokernel constructions (section Tag 01AF)

proof.text: For each literal subsheaf K in T, let i_K : K → M be its actual inclusion and take Q_K = cokernel(i_K), with q_K = cokernel.π(i_K), in the fixed-universe category of module sheaves. This cokernel exists by the abelian instance of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and [def-sp-abelian]. The cokernel cofork is colimiting and its projection is epic. This categorical cokernel realizes the sheafification of the sectionwise quotient described in the source.

source.place: Tag 01BC, lemma-set-isomorphism-classes-finite-type-modules, proof: parametrization by kernel subsheaves; Tag 01AG, lemma-abelian, and preceding kernel/cokernel constructions (section Tag 01AF)

proof.text: Fix an epimorphism p : M → N, and let A = kernel(p), i : A → M its kernel inclusion. The forgetful functor to presheaves of modules preserves finite limits, so i remains monic there; evaluation then makes every i_W injective. Define K(W) as the range submodule of i_W. Naturality of i proves restriction stability. Each i_W identifies A(W) linearly with K(W), and these identifications assemble into a presheaf isomorphism A.val ≅ K.toPresheafOfModules. Transfer the sheaf axiom from A along the underlying isomorphism of abelian presheaves. Full faithfulness of the forgetful functor lifts this to a module-sheaf isomorphism e : A ≅ K. Its hom followed by the literal inclusion equals i sectionwise. Transport the kernel universal property along e.symm to prove that the actual inclusion K → M is a kernel of p. This realizes the sectionwise kernel subsheaf of the source without reproving the gluing axiom.

source.place: Tag 01BC, lemma-set-isomorphism-classes-finite-type-modules, proof: parametrization by kernel subsheaves; Tag 01AG, lemma-abelian, and preceding kernel/cokernel constructions (section Tag 01AF)

proof.text: Apply the abelian-category theorem that an epimorphism is a cokernel of any of its kernels, Abelian.epiIsCokernelOfKernel, to p and the literal kernel fork from the preceding step. This is the normal-epimorphism argument in [def-sp-abelian], and gives a colimiting cokernel cofork whose projection is exactly p.

source.place: Tag 01BC, lemma-set-isomorphism-classes-finite-type-modules, proof: parametrization by kernel subsheaves; Tag 01AG, lemma-abelian, and preceding kernel/cokernel constructions (section Tag 01AF)

proof.text: The two cokernel properties, for $q_{\mathcal K}$ and for $p$, give unique maps $\psi:Q_{\mathcal K}\to\mathcal N$ and $\chi:\mathcal N\to Q_{\mathcal K}$ with $\psi q_{\mathcal K}=p$ and $\chi p=q_{\mathcal K}$. Therefore $(\chi\psi)q_{\mathcal K}=q_{\mathcal K}$ and $(\psi\chi)p=p$. Uniqueness in the respective cokernel universal properties gives $\chi\psi=1_{Q_{\mathcal K}}$ and $\psi\chi=1_{\mathcal N}$. Hence $\psi$ is an isomorphism with exactly $\psi\circ q_{\mathcal K}=p$, proving both clauses with $t=\mathcal K$.
